macosNotifications.title: Enable Notifications on macOS
macosNotifications.intro: Notifications are currently disabled in your system settings. Follow the steps below to enable them:
macosNotifications.step1: Open System Settings on your Mac.
macosNotifications.step2: Navigate to the Notifications section in the left sidebar.
macosNotifications.step3: Find and select the GSH Desktop application from the list.
macosNotifications.step4: Toggle the Allow Notifications switch on.
macosNotifications.tip: Tip: If the app does not appear in the list, close and reopen it to trigger its registration in the system.

chat.improveHarnessHint: Opens a chat that reads this conversation and proposes changes to the project's CLAUDE.md, skills and hooks, each with the evidence. You approve every edit.
chat.improveHarnessPrompt:
Improve this project's harness based on a previous conversation (session ${sessionId}).

1. Find the transcript: `ls ~/.claude/projects/*/${sessionId}.jsonl`. It is JSONL and can be large: use grep/jq/head, don't read it whole. Focus on the user's messages, the corrections they made, tool errors and rework.
2. Read the harness that applied there: CLAUDE.md (project and global), .claude/skills, .claude/agents, .claude/commands and the hooks in .claude/settings.json.
3. Find what cost time: a missing instruction, an ignored rule, a repeated step, a wrong command, something the user had to correct.
4. For each finding, propose ONE small change to the project's harness (the global one only if I ask):
   - stable fact about the repository → CLAUDE.md
   - multi-step procedure → skill
   - something that must be prevented → a hook that blocks and explains why it stopped and what to do instead
5. Before editing, show a table: what, where and the evidence (the moment in the conversation that justifies it). No evidence, no proposal. If nothing is worth it, say so.
6. Then apply one change at a time with Edit/Write; I review each diff and approve or deny it.

CLAUDE.md goes into every message: keep it short.

resources.farmDesc: Agent loops read from Claude Code transcripts.
resources.harnessFeatureDesc: Button that opens what the agent loads in the workspace: instructions, skills, subagents, hooks, permissions and MCP.
resources.teamFarmDesc: On the same network (e.g. at the office), each GSH announces its own farm and shows your teammates' next to yours — zoom out to see them. No server: nothing leaves the local network. Off, nothing leaves your GSH.
resources.teamNameDesc: Only people using the same team name see each other.
resources.teamMeDesc: Shown above your farm to your teammates.
resources.teamShowTitlesDesc: Titles may contain bits of your prompts. Off, teammates only see each agent's folder, status and tokens.
resources.teamSecretDesc: Turns on agent-to-agent messaging: your agent can send messages and files to your teammates' agents, and theirs to yours. Everyone on the team uses the same password; without it, nobody knocks on your door (and farms without it don't show up).
resources.teamDoorAllowDesc: Teammates' names, comma separated. Empty = the whole team.
resources.teamDoorAskDesc: When a teammate sends something to one of your agents, GSH asks you before handing it over. Off, your agent gets it directly, marked as information from a teammate (not as an order from you).
resources.teamNetworkDesc: The office network's IP range (e.g. 192.168.10.0/24). When set, GSH only announces and listens while you're on it.
resources.farmSceneryDesc: Where the agents live: the farm or a pixel art office.
resources.graphDesc: Visualize the agents of the workspace and who talks to whom.
resources.browserDesc: "Browser" tab in the pane menu (where the platform has an inline webview).
resources.agentIslandDesc: Pill at the top of the window with the gorilla: who is working, who is waiting for you, and permission requests you can answer right there.

designSystems.title: Design systems
designSystems.desc: In GSH these are the themes: interface, terminal and code colors in one package.

remoteHosts.title: Remote hosts
remoteHosts.description: Machines you reach over SSH. Adding a host here is the same as adding one from the workspace "+" menu.
remoteHosts.removeMessage: Remove "${name}" and all its workspaces? Nothing is deleted on the host itself.
remoteHosts.deviceKeyDesc: Add this public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the host so this device can connect.
remoteHosts.helpBody: GSH Desktop connects to your machine over SSH and talks to a small server that runs the terminals, files and git there. The host must have GSH Desktop (desktop) or the gsh-server installed and running, and this device’s public key added to its ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.
